Short Bio: Janine van Wyk
Football (Defender / Center-back)

Janine van Wyk is a monumental figure in South African football, widely revered as one of the greatest defenders to ever wear the national colors. A true servant of the game, she holds the remarkable distinction of being South Africa's most-capped footballer in history, amassing over 180 appearances for Banyana Banyana. Throughout her legendary career, she was the rock at the back, known for her commanding presence, crunching tackles, and powerful free-kicks. video_title: STILLE NAG in Moana Styl (Afrikaanse Kerslied Cover) 🇿🇦
description:
🌊 STILLE NAG IN DIE STYL VAN MOANA 🎶

🌙 Stille Nag (Silent  (Afrikaanse weergawe geïnspireer deur die magiese oseaanvibes van Disney se “Moana”)
Hierdie lied is pure vrede, heilige rustigheid en daai diep oseaan-kalmte wat jou laat voel asof die sterre en die see saam sing. “Stille Nag” word hier hergebore met Polinesiese ritmes, sagte tromme, oseaan-golwe op die agtergrond en ’n koor wat soos die voorvaders se stemme klink – net soos in Moana se epiese liedere. Dit bou stadig op met harmonieë, ukelele-agtige klanke en ’n hemelse vrouestem wat die heilige nag oor die eilande laat sweef.
Dis nie net ’n Kerslied nie. Dis ’n Afrikaanse ode aan die stil oseaan-nag waar die lig van die hemel die donker see verlig, en die geboorte van die Redder voel soos ’n nuwe reis oor die horison. 🌙✨
As jy al daai vibe gevoel het waar die see jou roep in die nag, en die sterre vertel van wonder en vrede, gaan hierdie een jou tref — reg in die siel.

🎧 Luister met oorfone aan. Volume sag vir die volle oseaan-rus. 🌺 Dink aan ’n Polinesiese eiland onder die sterrehemel. ❤️ Stille nag… laat die golwe dit dra.

For daily videos leading up to Christmas and a chance to vote on the next song for us to cover you can join the MLT Club here: https://monalisa-twins.com/mltclub/ 
We recorded and filmed “Time In A Bottle” during the first week of the MLT Club Advent Calendar. Our members voted for this beautiful song!

Each day, we documented the progress and showed it in a little video. From figuring out the guitar chords, to coming up with an arrangement, to finding a good filming location and then editing the video … we took the Club along for the whole very busy week!

Now we’re already working on the next pick, ”Daydream Believer" by The Monkees! If you want to be part of this Advent Calendar journey and help choose the final 3rd song, join the Club! :-)

There’ll also be a Club-exclusive Livestream on the 23rd with live music, giveaways, games and lots of chatting!

And, of course, you'll get to rewatch the past year's advent calendars, all the hundreds of behind-the-scenes videos, travel vlogs, reaction videos, vinyl listening sessions and photos posts we did over the years.

Thanks and groovy Christmas season!

Edelweiss  - The Sound Of Music Soundtrack Cover

-------------------

Did you know that “Edelweiss” is the national flower of Austria? It grows high up in the mountains in the Alps and is a “protected species”, so you are not allowed to pick it if you are lucky enough to encounter one in the wild.

When the song-writing team Rodgers and Hammerstein composed the music for the musical “Sound Of Music” they composed “Edelweiss” from scratch. So contrary to what a lot of people think it is not actually a traditional Austrian folk song and was purely written for the 1959 musical. But it could be and we like it! Seeing as we two are Austrians, it seemed right to cover it, don’t you think?

description:
Jacobus (Koos) Johannes du Plessis (10 May 1945 – 15 January 1984) was a prominent South African singer-songwriter and poet, colloquially known as Koos Doep. Although he received critical acclaim for much of his work, he became best known for the runaway success of a rendition of his song "Kinders van die Wind" ("Children of the Wind") by Laurika Rauch.

Koos du Plessis was born in Rustenburg. He was the oldest of five children, and grew up in the mining town of Springs. After school, he attended the University of Pretoria, and the University of the Witwatersrand, majoring in Afrikaans-Nederlands (Afrikaans-Dutch). At university he met his future wife, Mornay. The couple had three daughters, Irma, Karen and Karla. Koos would eventually write a song for each of these four women in his life.

Koos worked as journalist and editor for several Afrikaans publications (Oggendblad, Die Vaderland, Die Nataller and Die Transvaler). He died in a motorcar accident close to Krugersdorp during the early morning hours of 15 January 1984.
Legacy in Afrikaans
In 2010 two Koos du Plessis tribute albums were released in The Netherlands posthumously. First was Ofschaaid Zunder Woorden, an album with songs of Du Plessis sung in Grunnegs by Wia Buze and Klaas Spekken. Karla du Plessis joined for a special duet on this album. Second was Die Land Van Blou Saffiere, released in the Tussen Kontinente-series. This release was a hardcover book that included a biography, lyrics with footnotes and explanations and a CD with 20 of his songs. He wrote two religious songs: Gebed (Prayer: Let me never leave this ground, let me in thy shadow stay...) and a carol Somerkersfees (Summer Christmas). The latter was incorporated into the hymnals of several Afrikaans churches.

In 1965, the song began to attract airplay at radio stations in Boston and throughout Florida. The growing airplay led Tom Wilson, the song's producer, to remix the track, overdubbing electric instruments and drums. This remixed version was released as a single in September 1965. The remix hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 for the week ending January 1, 1966, leading the duo to reunite and hastily record their second album, which Columbia titled Sounds of Silence in an attempt to capitalize on the song's success. The remixed single version of the song was included on this follow-up album. Later, it was featured in the 1967 film The Graduate and was included on the film's soundtrack album. "Seemann (Deine Heimat ist das Meer)" (English translation "Sailor (Your Home is the Sea)") is a song originally written in German by Werner Scharfenberger (de) and lyricist Fini Busch (de). A 1959 German-language recording by Lolita became an international hit in 1960–61.

The song was covered in a number of languages, most notably by Petula Clark who had her first #1 UK hit with the English-language rendering "Sailor". Clark was also afforded international success with both "Sailor" and the French-language rendering "Marin". A rival version by Anne Shelton was a Top Ten UK hit, concluding her chart career. Other singers for whom "Sailor (Your Home is the Sea)" brought success as rendered in various languages include: Scandinavian singers Thory Bernhards and Towa Carson "Sjöman" (Swedish) and Jan Høiland "Sjömann" (Norwegian); Caterina Valente, who had a Flemish hit with "Zeeman (Je verlangen is de zee)"( Dutch;) a 1981 hit in the Netherlands for Ciska Peters (nl); and Virginia Lee (af) whose "Seeman" (Afrikaans) was a successful local cover in South Africa.

description:
La Paloma cover by Dawie Lindner on Yamaha psr SX700 keybord.

"La Paloma", "The Dove" in English, is a popular Spanish song that has been produced and reinterpreted in diverse cultures, settings, arrangements, and recordings over the last 140 years. The song was composed and written by the Spanish composer from the Basque region Sebastián Iradier (later Yradier) in the 1850s. In 1879, it was registered at the copyright office in Madrid as a "Canción Americana con acompañamiento de Piano".[1] Iradier was to die in obscurity within few years, never to learn how popular his song would become.

Very quickly, "La Paloma" became popular outside of Spain, particularly in Mexico, and soon spread around the world. In many places, including Afghanistan, Cuba, Colombia, Hawaii, the Philippines, Germany, Romania, Venezuela, Zanzibar, and Goa it gained the status of a quasi-folk song. Over the years, the popularity of "La Paloma" has surged and receded periodically, but never subsided. It may be considered one of the first universal popular hits and has appealed to artists of diverse musical backgrounds. There are more than one thousand versions of this song, and together with "Yesterday" by The Beatles, is one of the most-recorded songs in the history of music; it is certainly the most-recorded Spanish song.

description:
A heartfelt cross-cultural tribute connecting the soulful sounds of Joy Denalane with the timeless South African lullaby tradition. We explore the emotional depth of "Süsser Freund" and "Slaap My Kindjie," blending German soul with Afrikaans heritage. ✨🌍
Fun Facts to Connect Themes 💡
Soul Bridges: Joy Denalane is a pioneer of German Soul, often blending her heritage into her music, much like how this cover blends Afrikaans and German lullabies 🎶🇿🇦🇩🇪.

The Lullaby Connection: "Slaap My Kindjie" is the Afrikaans version of Brahms' Lullaby, which shares its structural DNA with the "Guten Abend, gut’ Nacht" featured in German classical lieder 🌹💤.

video_title: 🇿🇦 Sarie Marais: A Tribute to Mimi Coertse & The Legacy of Virginia Davids
description:
A deep-dive cover of the classic "Sarie Marais," performed as a heartfelt tribute to the legendary Mimi Coertse. 🎭 This rendition honors the lineage of South African vocal excellence—from Virginia Davids’ iconic 1994 performance at the State Theatre to the global stages of the MET with Pretty Yende. 🎵 Exploring the history of the "Grootrivier" through a modern, textured lens. 🌊✨

Fun Facts

Vocal Lineage: Virginia Davids, a powerhouse of the Black Tie Ensemble, mentored Pretty Yende, who eventually took that South African brilliance to the Metropolitan Opera (MET). 🏛️✨

The "Grootrivier": The lyrics mention "Upington se sand," referring to the Orange River (Grootrivier). Upington was a vital refuge and remains a symbol of the rugged Northern Cape landscape. 🍇🏜️

Sarie Marais: While known as a folk song, it’s actually a story of longing and displacement, making the dry, atmospheric textures of this cover a perfect fit for the "Upington sand" theme. 📜💨

description:
So it has been about a week since I've uploaded my "goodbye" video, and here I'm officially saying, I'm back in business!

I'm going to keep that video up because it did mark the end of the first chapter of this channel. 

This new chapter will include a lot of pop, rock and worship music. I'm moving away from most metal music, in particular metal that resembles the occult. 

For a long time, I thought that lyrics don't affect me in any way. But the truth is, there is power in the words that we speak and listen to, and I'm choosing not to expose myself or any of my viewers with lyrics of that destructive nature.

I'm not saying metal is completely banned from my channel. The best solos and riffs are found in metal music, and I will continue to highlight that aspect of the genre!

I'm also planning to release much more original music, so stay tuned for that!

Regards
Mr A

video_title: You’re The Voice - Perpetuum Jazzile (#stayathome corona quarantine videocall vocal orchestra cover)
description:
Creative: 37 Singers' STAY-AT-HOME Shout Out!

Dear Coronavirus, 
Here's a message from Perpetuum Jazzile: “We're not gonna sit in silence, we're not gonna live with fear! This time we know we all can stand together. With the power to be powerful, believin' we can make it better.” // Koronavirus, tule imaš sporočilo Perpetuum Jazzile: "Ne bomo sedeli v tišini in ne bomo živeli v strahu. Tokrat vemo, da lahko vsi stopimo skupaj. Z močjo najmočnejših in z zaupanjem, da bomo vse to presegli."

Dear friends, 
This video is our response to the situation we're all facing and a gift to you all. Since we're amidst preparation for a new show, but following the rule: STAY AT HOME unable to get together to rehearse, we got another idea how to harmonize remotely. It took literally 3 days to pull this off – first using our phones at home, then every singer's audio and video footage was put together – and we are pretty pleased with the result. What do you think? // Dragi prijatelji! Ta video je naš odgovor na situacijo, v kateri smo se vsi skupaj znašli, in naše darilo vsem vam. ker smo sredi priprav na nov show, a moramo slediti zapovedi OSTANI DOMA, zaradi česar ne moremo na skupne vaje, smo prišli na idejo, da bi se uglasili na daljavo. Trajalo je vsega 3 dni, da smo ta posnetek izpeljali - in kar zadovoljni smo z rezultatom. Kaj menite?

With the song "You're The Voice" we want to connect people in self-isolation around the world, inspire them with music and remind them that every person is a voice of reason that can make a change. Let's go! // S skladbo "You're The Voice" ("Ti si glas") želimo povezati vse ljudi v samoizolaciji po svetu, jih navdihniti z našo glasbo in nas vse spomniti, da vsak človek lahko predstavlja glas razuma, ki pripelje do spremembe. Dajmo! 

Stay strong and #stayathome! // Ostanimo močni in DOMA!

***

Look What They've Done To My Song, Ma - Melanie Safka Cover by MonaLisa Twins

We vaguely remember covering this song on a radio station many, many years ago but hadn’t played it since. That’s until we decided to revisit it for a Duo Session! We love this song and Melanie’s music in general. “Look, What They’ve Done To My Song, Ma” is one of those quirky gems from the past.

We’ve done “Michelle” by the Beatles (on our very first live album) and now “Look, What They’ve Done To My Song, Ma” … we think you’ve heard us butcher the French language enough now, we’ll probably leave it at that. Unless you can think of other songs with French lyrics that we really need to cover? We do apologise to all the Frenchmen, lol.

We’ve recorded a lot more Duo Sessions over at the MLT Club (http://www.mlt1.uk/ytmltc) and will soon release the new Duo Session II album! Watch this space 😃

A huge shoutout and thank you to Journey Instruments (https://journeyinstruments.com/) for providing us with these stunning instruments. Believe it or not, this guitar and bass can both be folded in half and fit neatly into a bag the size of a backpack. If you’re in the market for a (travel) guitar or bass, definitely give them some consideration, they have lots of models to choose from.

Thanks for listening, this was a fun one to film!
Mona & Lisa

“She Loves You” … The UK’s best-selling single of the 60s. If you had to describe the British invasion or Beatlemania in one song, “She Loves You” would be a pretty darn good pick, wouldn’t you agree?

The Beatles and the Cavern Club go hand in hand. After all, if it wasn't for the Beatles who played in the original Cavern Club nearly 300 times, it would not have earned its nickname "the most famous club in the world". 

So when we had the opportunity to play there 100 times between 2014 and 2016, we always made sure to pack as many Beatles tunes into our setlist as we could. After all, they were the reason so many people visited this Club, every single day of the year.

While we didn't stick to a "Beatles only" setlist and snuck plenty of other covers and our originals into the mix, we still made sure every Beatles fan who attended would leave the place feeling satisfied. And "She Loves You" was always a fan favourite :-)

It’s one of those songs that’s way more complex than it seems, and to make it sound good at the Cavern was trickier than it might look on video. But we loved it. A classic, important tune that definitely belonged on the set list.

We hope you enjoy the video,

Mona & Lisa

-------------

Hello friends,

We want to wish you a Merry Christmas by sharing a new video with you. Our cover of "Junk" was originally recorded for the MLT Club a few months ago but today seemed fitting to post it on YouTube so everyone can watch it.

Paul wrote the song while the Beatles were still together but released it two years later on his first solo album in 1970. It's one of those songs that we have hummed to ourselves hundreds of times over the years but still remember how, when we first heard this song, it took our breath away. It’s Paul McCartney at his best. The melody, the chord progression, the subject matter, the way he manages to sing about something so deep in an incredibly light, moving and poetic way. It is one of those perfect songs.

Having loved this song for so long now, recording it properly as a Duo Session felt only right. It's a song as beautiful as they come, and we tried our best to capture the nostalgic, enchanting feeling that the original recording gives us.

"Christmas is the season of giving" they say but who says that can't be experiences, quality time, friendship and love ... because all that other stuff may one day end up being junk in the yard ...

🎙️ Sobre Rafael Santos
Rafael Santos Díaz es cantante, compositor y actor colombiano, e hijo del ícono del vallenato Diomedes Díaz. Desde los 18 años ha construido una carrera propia dentro del género, trabajando con importantes acordeoneros como Alvarito López. Su estilo mezcla tradición y frescura, consolidándolo como una figura clave del vallenato actual. También ha participado como actor en la novela Rafael Orozco, el ídolo, donde interpretó un personaje basado en su padre.


🎙️ Sobre Jimmy Zambrano
Jimmy Zambrano es un reconocido acordeonista colombiano con una trayectoria que abarca décadas. Inició su carrera en Venezuela y se destacó por su trabajo con Los Diablitos y posteriormente con Jorge Celedón, con quien grabó nueve álbumes y ganó un Latin Grammy en 2007. Su estilo combina virtuosismo, sensibilidad y una profunda conexión con las raíces del vallenato.

Pink Floyd - it's hard not to love them or at least respect them for their ground breaking original style, profound lyrics, themed albums, ...

We've been into Pink Floyd since our teenage years. We even went to see Roger Water's "The Wall" tour back in 2013 and left the stadium mesmerised and floating on a natural high.

Yet we have never covered one of their songs.

We sure learned the solo parts for "Another Brick In The Wall" and worked hard on the smooth bends and fluent runs, but most of their songs didn't lend themselves too well to be covered by 2 guitarists or a 4 piece rock 'n' roll band.

But then there's "Wish You Were Here". A song with a purported backstory so sad that it's hard not to get emotional when reading up on it. A tragic masterpiece, partially inspired by their lost band member Syd Barrett (or at least open to interpretation).

We thought it would be a great choice for a duo session ...  

He hope you like this one! ♥

Mona & Lisa

Here’s a cover of one of our favourite non-Beatles Beatles songs! Till There Was You - From the musical “The Music Man”, covered by the Beatles back in ‘63. We can’t think of many songs with a melody sweeter than this one. 

Dedicated to our friend Steve, who we lost this Winter. It was one of his favourite songs and today would be his Birthday ♥

We often reminisce about the time when we "caught the Beatle bug" in our early teens and would experience our very own Beatlemania together with our best friend from high school. 
When the three of us first saw the video of the Beatles doing this song for the Royal Variety Performance we just about lost our minds and immediately fell in love with it - Paul surely knew what he was doing with all that cute head bobbing! 

For several weeks to follow we would sing this song to ... no, AT anyone who would listen.  During gym class, in the locker rooms (great acoustics!), at the bus stop and even in the tram on the way back from school. We couldn't get the pretty melody (that includes George's stunning solo) out of our heads. 

Our guitar teacher at the time even transcribed the guitar parts for us although they were a little too advanced for us at the time. We still tried! 

Ten years later, and after learning that it was one of Steve's favourite songs too, we want to try it again.

We hope you'll enjoy the song and video. Let us know if you have any memories connected to the song yourself!

Much love to you all,
Mona & Lisa

We filmed this cover of "Starman" on the Martian looking volcanic island that is Lanzarote during our trip there in January. It was the perfect setting. Every time we left the house it was impossible not to expect a UFO to take off behind one of those outlandish looking volcanoes.

We've always been fascinated with space and the question of what could be "out there", ever since we were little kids. Our dad always used to tell us a made-up ongoing bed-time story over several years. It was about two kids, Johnny and Clarissa, and their intergalactic friends, travelling through the universe, exploring new planets and meeting starmen on wild adventures.

Naturally, that planted a strong curiosity about everything outerspacey and we've loved “Starman” ever since we first heard it and were old enough to understand the English lyrics. It captures our feelings about the vast and mysterious universe spot on.

Needless to say, we loved working on this song!

Please let us know what you think of the new "Starman" video in the comments section on YouTube or right here underneath this post. It's the first time we've done a Bowie cover and we're curious to hear everyone's thoughts.

They say nothing is more constant than change. So true, as again, an old year has come to an end, and we used the remaining, quieter days after Christmas to reflect on the past and think about what’s to come.

description:
I'M BACK HOME!!! I had a nice visit with my family, but it's nice to be uploading a video once again!

It was approximately a 10 hour drive yesterday, and what better thing to do first do you get home than a nice King Diamond cover!

When I was on the road I thought about the channel a lot... I'm gonna keep doing these thumbnails simply because I like making them and I really like the HD videos (which I initially rejected) I have going on too. As for the playing part of it I'm going to head back to my roots, where I mostly did first takes only and didn't care too much about getting everything perfect. 

Obviously I'm not going to purposefully make my videos terrible, but the goal since the beginning was to be a channel unlike any other on YouTube. A channel that only does videos through my selfie camera and phone's microphone, one that isn't afraid to show flaws and one that won't subject itself to predictable perfect videos every time.

I'm certain there's a even larger audience for what I'm going for, and I'm sure I'll reach a lot of new people in the new year!

For the people that watched my videos this year, I seriously can't thank you enough!

Now, about this video, I'm sure you know by know my drums have a limited recording capacity. I literally just told myself skrew it I'm gonna play till it stops lmao.

Happy New Year!!!

In November 2015 we joined Steve Harley & Cockney Rebel for their 16-dates 'Best Years Of Our Lives' 40th Anniversary Tour. It was an fantastic experience and we had a terrific time on the road.
While rehearsing for the tour we decided it was only fitting to cover our favourite song and at the same time title track of the album "The Best Years Of Our Lives". We consider the live performance of this song, especially the one on Steve's first live album "Face to Face" one of the most touching live moments in rock history. It clearly shows why he belongs to the exclusive circle of live entertainers who can mesmerise an audience in style without having to play cheap tricks. 

Love and stay groovy,
Mona and Lisa

RIP Phil Everly!
We are very sad that Phil from the "Everly Brothers" passed away yesterday!

We first got into their music about three or four years ago and covered their song "All I Have To Do Is Dream" soon after (http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AQAO6iao00U). When we were deciding on covers to play with our band last year, we knew for sure that we wanted to include one of their songs! They were great and influential songwriters who created some true masterpieces! To honor Phil's work and to give him and his brother back some of the love they shared with the world, we quickly cut together a video today of us performing "Wake Up Little Susie" at a concert about a year ago. 

All our prayers go out to their family and friends, especially to Don Everly, who has lost his brother and musical partner.
Phil, may you be happy and free wherever you are right now!

Mona & Lisa

This video is for Steve, one of the most generous, supporting people we have ever had the luck to encounter.
 
In summer 2013, during our stay in London, we shot a music video for our song "When We're Together", in which we painted a huge picture, together with passing strangers in the busy main road of Camden. 

Later we auctioned the painting, and after some shipping difficulties with the original highest bidder, Steve from Miami finally bought the canvas and put it up in his office. We were happy that the painting has finally found a new home, and because of the nice messages and pictures his secretary Mary had sent us, we knew it was in good hands with lovely people.

After that he wanted to support us and our music even more, in a way that completely blew our minds, still does and always will! Look at all those wonderful guitars!

He wants nothing in return except for us to continue making music and making good use of the instruments he sent us. So we were looking for a project in which we could play all the guitars and at the same time thank him for his generosity. 

We kept close contact with Mary, who told us that one of his favorite songs was "This Boy" by the Beatles, a tune we too absolutely adore! So we spent the last couple of days in the studio and recorded the song and used only the guitars Steve had sent us. The nice bass line was played by our lovely Dad who this time refused to be in the video :P (We'll get him again for the next studio cover recording ;) )

We hope that you, Steve

In this tribute to the Health Workers by Wouter Kellerman and The Mzansi Youth Choir from Soweto, these lines from “The Climb” describe the character of the Health Workers worldwide. Despite the dangers, they are climbing very steep mountains to summit the top, but the next morning there is another and even higher mountain awaiting them...and then another.

Above your masks, your eyes project hope, determination, but also deep sadness and true empathy.  With our music and in Miley Cyrus’s words, we want to encourage you..

And Guns N Roses for writing an awesome song!

video_title: Moise Mbiye - Ye Oyo (Here she is) | Cover | ft. Gabriel Okota | A Natsa Creations Film
description:
Here's an extract from my cover of Moise Mbiye's song Ye Oyo (Here she is) Covered by Jonathan Kalombo ft  Gabriel Okota on Guitar. 

Please do subscribe. Thank you for watching, stay blessed!!!

Translation of Song meaning (comes from the original video, link at the bottom):
English:
The song is the story of a person who is presenting to God a person who is not perfect, but his/her heart loves and asks God to change this person so that his/her love's weaknesses become strengths.
They also that their family  supports them so they stay together in peace for a long time. They also ask the church to pray for them so they can be blessed.
The chorus translates pretty much as I have sung it in English:
"Here she is, my lover, here she is, I dreamt it in a dream, my prayers have been answered hey, Here she is no more hiding, here she is, despite the struggles here she is..."

French:
La chanson est l'histoire d'une personne qui présente à Dieu quelqu'un avec des défauts, mais dont le coeur aime; afin qu'Il fasse grâce en transformant  ses faiblesses en force. 

Ensuite c'est à la famille qu'elle fait les présentations  en leur demandant de les aider à rester longtemps ensemble et en paix. C’est à l’église que les présentations s’achèvent, en leur demandant de prier pour eux afin d’être béni. 

Traduction refrain:

Le voici, c'est mon amour. Je l'avais vu dans mon rêve, ma prière a agit. 
Le voici, il n'y a plus des cachotteries, malgré les tempêtes, le voici.

____________________________________________________________

Label: Bibomba Music
Auteur compositeur: Past. Moise Mbiye.

This is the first of the 3 live videos of me finally getting to perform with these two amazing musicians and friends of mine! Dieudonne Lusengu on lead guitar and Junior Baloji on Bass! I can’t wait to share the other two with you! Shout out to Paul Kumirai for such great production work!

The song is a cover, originally sung by Pasteur Yannick N’tumba. The message is a testimony of being given a new life by Jesus such that “The stone that the builder's rejected has become the cornerstone.” (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0rwuct5xzMI )

Thank you for watching, please do subscribe, comment and share!

Stay Blessed! 😊

description:
Hello Bonjour!!! 😊

“Sukola Ngai” means Cleanse me in Lingala! This is one of my favorite songs to perform live. The overall message is gratitude to Jesus for cleansing our hearts so that we may be saved! I’ll probably post a few more performances of it and hopefully with backing vocals!
It is a cover, originally sung by Denis Ngonde and Carlyto Lassa. Two legendary Congolese gospel musicians!

Thank you for watching, please do subscribe, comment and share!

Stay Blessed! 😊

video_title: Ozzy Osbourne - Mama, I'm Coming Home (Guitar Solo Cover)
description:
The goal for this channel is to only post videos like this. I refuse to get better production or editing or thumbnails etc. I feel that almost every other cover channel on YouTube is so perfected that almost makes it a shame in my opinion. I do every part one take, every time and if I make mistakes so be it! And if that means not many people will watch my videos, I'm also fine with that. As long as I eventually gather a small audience that's more than enough. 

Such a tasty solo from Zakk Wylde. And yes, No More Tears is my favorite Ozzy album. So many great tracks! 

I played and recorded the drums beforehand on a Alessis Nitro Mesh kit if you're wondering.

video_title: When the Cover Version Has More SOUL Than the ORIGINAL... | The Voice Kids
description:

video_title: It Started Out So Nice by Sixto Rodriguez - cover with chords lyrics
description:
It Started Out So Nice by Sixto Rodriguez off his Coming From Reality Album - After The Fact - as sung by me. Not my best rendition - a few timing issues,(maar nou ja...) but enjoy the effort of added chords with lyrics. Earphones on full volume might be helpful as the upload seems 'soft' for some reason
And no, that's not a fart near the end of the video :-)
I wouldn't have a clue what this song is about but the visual poetry of the lyrics and quirky character names makes it interesting. I enjoy playing it from time to time. If you DO know what this song is about, feel free to share it with us as there's not a lot on the web about it. Thanks for watching and hope you enjoyed. 

Update: 24 January 2014. Duroc = rare breed of pig. 
                                      Durok = Russian card game 
                                                  A village in Poland

video_title: Hey Baby - Refiloe Jane Tribute | SA Heroes Series (LeLi Cover)
description:
Onstuitbaar op die sokkerveld en 'n ware inspirasie vir die hele land! In hierdie episode van ons SA Heldenaarsreeks vier ons die briljante Refiloe Jane—kaptein, stryder en trots van Banyana Banyana.

Om hulde te bring aan haar energie en impak, gee ons 'n unieke, vrolike en sielvolle draai aan DJ Ötzi se klassieker "Hey Baby", met 'n spesiale tweetalige (Afrikaans en isiXhosa) verwerking wat elke hart laat saamsing:

Hey, hey mntwana... Ndifuna ukwazi... Ukuba uya kuba yintombi yam...
Hey, hey baba... Ek wil weet... Of jy my meisie sal wees...

Gemaak in ons kenmerkende 9:16-formaat met 'n warm, vintage esteties vir die gemeenskap.

video_title: Maak gereed vir hoendervleis! Gerda Steyn Tribute | Sarie Marais (Mimi Sings)
description:
Maak gereed vir hoendervleis! In hierdie spesiale Vrouedag-uitgawe van ons SA Heldenaarsreeks bring ons hulde aan die merkwaardige Gerda Steyn—die onstuitbare koningin van die Comrades en die pad wat ons almal met trots vervul. Haar uithouvermoë en passie is 'n inspirasie vir elke Suid-Afrikaner.

Om hierdie eerbetoon te kroon, bring Mimi Sings 'n diep ontroerende, akustiese vertolking van die klassieke volksliedjie "Sarie Marais", gevul met nostalgie en egte landswydse trots.

Gemaak met 'n warm, vintage esteties en 'n egte 9:16-visuele styl vir ons gemeenskap.

description:

Τόσα χρόνια μες στους χάρτες μου σε ψάχνω, 
κι ας μην έσκυψες ποτέ στο μέτωπό μου με τα δυο σου χείλια 
ν' αφήσεις μια ανάσα στη ζωή μου. 
Κι αν η προσευχή μου οινόπνευμα μυρίζει, καπνό και πυρετό, 
στο γυάλινο το κύμα τ' όνομά σου 
φωνάζω να καθρεφτιστεί η φωνή μου. 

Και στην όχθη που χτενίζεσαι ακούστει σαν αλμυρό 
τραγούδι που σου φέρνει ερωτευμένο το νερό. 
Και στο διάβολο πουλάω τη ψυχή μου εγώ, για να βρεθώ 
απόψε τυλιγμένος στου κορμιού σου το βυθό. 

Κάπου η νύχτα μεσοπέλαγα κρεμιέται στην αγχόνη τ' ουρανού 
κι ο δαίμονας καβάλα στο σκοτάδι 
αρπάζει τη μετέωρη ευχή μου. 
Και σαν άστρο καυτερό προς το νησί σου τα λόγια μου πετάει πληγώνοντας τα βράχια και την άμμο, 
στη χτένα σου καρφώνει την ψυχή μου. 

Και σταγόνα τη σταγόνα κυλάω εγώ σαν αλμυρό 
νερό στους ώμους και στον ακριβό σου το λαιμό. 
Κι ας το ξέρω πως του λόγου του στην ανεμόσκαλα εκεί, 
με περιμένει για να μου λιμάρει το σκοινί. 

Πάνε χρόνια που αντίκρυ αναβοσβήνουν τα φώτα κάποιας γης, 
τα φώτα κάποιας ξεχασμένης νήσου, 
που λένε είν' οι κορφές του παραδείσου. 
Μα το ξέρω είναι της θάλασσας τα μάγια, δεν υπάρχει αυτή η στεριά, 
μιας και κανείς ποτέ του εκεί δεν πήγε, 
γι' αυτό σφιχτά κρατιέμαι στο κορμί σου. 

Και μπροστά απ' τους κολασμένους περνάω εγώ σαν μια σκιά 
που σεργιανάει στον Άδη τη δικιά σου μυρωδιά. 
Κι είναι λέω ο παράδεισος για μας, αγάπη μου μικρή, 
να μοιραζόμαστε τούτη τη κόλαση μαζί.

video_title: The Ballad of the Green Berets Cover Dawie Lindner
description:
"The Ballad of the Green Berets" is a patriotic song in the ballad style about the United States Army Special Forces. It is one of the few popular songs of the Vietnam War years to cast the military in a positive light. In 1966 it became a major hit, reaching No. 1 for five weeks on the Hot 100 and four weeks on Cashbox. It was also a crossover hit, reaching No. 1 on Billboard's Easy Listening chart and No. 2 on Billboard's Country survey. Billboard ranked it No. 10 in its year-end chart for 1966,[3] while it tied for first with "California Dreamin'" by the Mamas and the Papas in Cash Box's year-end rankings.[4]

The song was written by then-Staff Sergeant or "SSG" Barry Sadler, beginning when he was training to be a Special Forces medic. The author Robin Moore, who wrote the book The Green Berets, helped Sadler write the lyrics and get a recording contract with RCA Records. The demo of the song was produced in a rudimentary recording studio at Fort Liberty, with the help of Gerry Gitell and LTG William P. Yarborough.[5]

The lyrics were written, in part, in honor of U.S. Army Specialist 5 James Gabriel Jr., a Special Forces operator and the first native Hawaiian to die in Vietnam, who was killed by Viet Cong gunfire while on a training mission with the South Vietnamese Army on April 8, 1962.[6] One verse mentioned Gabriel by name, but it was not used in the recorded version.[7]

Sadler recorded the song and eleven other tunes in New York in December 1965. The song and album, Ballads of the Green Berets, were released in January 1966. He performed the song on television on January 30, 1966 on The Ed Sullivan Show, and on other TV shows including Hollywood Palace and The Jimmy Dean Show.

Herholdt was born in the small Gauteng mining village of Nigel and at the age of three made her first singing performance at the local community recreation hall, singing the Afrikaans lullaby Slaap, my Kindjie.

Career
Her breakthrough came when she did a spot on Gwynneth Ashley Robin's show and was soon asked to record Ek Verlang Na Jou.[2] The single went gold in South Africa, selling over 25 000 copies.[3]

Her subsequent albums and singles earned her similar critical and commercial success. She went on to win a total of eight Sarie awards.[2] In the 1970s and 1980s, she was frequently the best-selling female artist in South Africa.[2]

In 1979, she finally fulfilled her ambition to act by starring in Sing vir die Harlekyn, and winning a Rapport Oscar-Award as Best Female Newcomer.[1]

She later enjoyed music success in Europe, she holds the distinction of being the first ever South African singer to be invited to perform in the Netherlands on their local Television.[6] She recorded her song Oberammergau in Dutch. She also performed in Belgium, pushing Oberammergau into fifth place in the Belgian charts.[3]

In 1989, she performed at the Religious Broadcasting Corporation in Washington, coinciding with the release of her gospel album, The Warrior is a Child.[3]

In 1991, she received an award from the Afrikaans Chamber of Commerce for her services to Afrikaans music.[2]

In 1995, she signed an album contract with BMG Records, enjoying success with the title track of her new BMG compilation, Skipskop. Her 1998 album Ritsel in die Rietbos did not meet critical and commercial expectations. But she rebounded with the critically acclaimed 2000 album, Reconstructing Alice.[3]

In 2002 she developed her own record company, Son Music and released Sonjare, a nostalgic retrospective of her original hits

Ein Stern (... that bears your name) is a hit song by the Austrian singer Nikolaus Presnik alias Nik P. from 1998. It became a hit in the party hit version by the Austrian singer DJ Ötzi together with Nik P. in the German-speaking countries and leads (together with Butterfly by Danyel Gérard ) the all-time list of the most successful singles in German chart history (256 points each). 

The song was written and composed by Nikolaus Presnik in 1998. Interpreted by Michael Stern , it took part in the Grand Prix des Schlagers in the same year and reached tenth place there.

It was widely played in Mallorca 's club scene at the end of 2006 , bringing it to new prominence as a party hit . It was then released in February 2007 in the version by DJ Ötzi together with Nik P. as the first single from DJ Ötzi's album Sternstunden and reached number one in the German and Austrian charts and number two in the Swiss charts .  Four years after the success of the Burger Dance , DJ Ötzi scored another number one hit in Germany with Ein Stern and , after Anton from Tirol (1999), his second hit, which also appeared inAustria reached number one in the charts .

With 108 weeks in the German charts, it is one of the songs that stayed in the German singles charts the longest . At the time of publication, he set a new record. It was also the first piece to be in the German charts for more than two years. In the RTL channel 's Ultimate Chart Show , the song was placed at number 1 of the "most successful songs of the new millennium". 

With more than 1.2 million units sold, the single has been certified four times platinum in Germany, making it one of the best-selling German hits and one of the best-selling singles in Germany in general . 

Even before DJ Ötzi and Nik P. released the song together, the Duisburg singer Nic was able to place himself in the single charts with his version Eine Stern .

video_title: Sewen Spanish Angels   Cover   Dawie Lindner
description:
"Seven Spanish Angels" is a song written by Troy Seals and Eddie Setser, and recorded by Ray Charles as a duet with Willie Nelson. It was released in November 1984 as a single from Charles' 1984 album Friendship. Charles and Nelson split the verses, with Charles singing the first and Nelson the second, Charles sang the first and second choruses with Nelson joining for the outro. It was also included on Nelson's 1985 compilation album Half Nelson. "Seven Spanish Angels" was the most successful of Charles' eight hits on the country chart. The single spent one week at number one and a total of twelve weeks on the country chart.

Setser had suggested the title "Seven Spanish Angels" and he and Seals had written the song as a homage to the tejano flavored classic hits of Marty Robbins exemplified by Robbins' career record "El Paso" (Troy Seals quote): "When we finished it we thought 'Who in the world's gonna do it?' because Marty was [deceased]." Within two days "Seven Spanish Angels" had been successfully pitched to Willie Nelson. Before Nelson was able to record it, producer Billy Sherrill happened to hear the demo and wanted the song for Ray Charles. Sherrill proposed that Nelson and Charles duet on the song after learning of Nelson's having reserved it.

The song was Lobo's highest charting hit on the Billboard Hot 100 chart, where it spent two weeks at No. 2 in November. The single was the second of four of his songs to hit No. 1 on the Easy Listening chart, where it had a one-week stay at that top spot in December 1972. It became a gold record.

When released in the United Kingdom in 1972, the song failed to reach the UK Singles Chart; however, a re-release of the single in 1974, on the UK record label, peaked at No. 5.

The song also topped the music charts in at least seven nations, including Australia (Kent Music Report, two weeks), Canada (RPM Magazine, one week), and Germany (Media Control Charts, 13 weeks in 1973-1974).

Intieme, beeldryke Afrikaans lirieke

video_title: Do it Anyway - Alex Boye' Ft. Carmen Rasmusen Herbert (Vegas Tribute)
description:
CARMEN

My husband and I were just there-at Mandalay Bay-only a few days before. We watched a show. We walked the strip. Had a great time.

 Days later, I woke up to an alert on my phone-Breaking News on the Las Vegas mass shooting. For a second I wondered if I was still dreaming-this couldn’t really be happening again. My heart hurt. I felt sick. And I didn’t want to get out of bed. My husband and I said a prayer together and throughout the morning a song kept playing in my head: “Anyway” by Martina McBride. The lyrics struck me in a way they never had and I had a thought to call my friend Alex Boye’ and record it. Right away. I always wonder “What can I do?” when disaster strikes. I always pray for comfort and healing, but I wanted to do more. To share some of what I was feeling in the best way I knew how-by singing. I hope that whoever listens to this will feel some tiny ray of hope, that when horrible things happen, you fight, you stay strong, you still dream, you still love, you still sing. This world can be so dark and it’s hard to believe the light will continue to shine. Believe it anyway.

ALEX 
What lies in the heart of a person who chooses to take 50+ lives at a concert, and was clearly hoping to have taken many more? Condolences to the families of these innocent victims who's lives will now have changed forever. May they find the kind of peace that surpasses all understanding through this that only God can give...Music is more than just entertainment. Music is our medicine. Right @marieosmond ? (We shot a music video together on the strip last year) NOW IT'S TIME TO INCREASE THE DOSAGE!!! No matter what they do, the music will never stop playing, and even if we have no instruments, it will keep playing in our hearts. R.I.P Quinton Robbins.

Please share!  #playforvegas #prayforvegas #route91love #routeninetyonelove

Teach Your Children - Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young

-------------

We might be biased but this Duo Session is the one that’s most precious to us. It has been 15 years since we last performed music together with our Dad like that. We do jam in the studio from time to time, and obviously we work in the studio together all the time but this was something different.

We used to play this song as just the two of us many, many years ago when we were teenagers, but we don’t think we ever grasped its full meaning until many years later. It’s one of those songs that hits different once you grow up!

A poignant masterpiece by Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young, and to be able to do the 3-part harmonies together with Dad means a lot to us.

We couldn’t wish for a better father and if there’s one thing he has done for us it’s to instil the bravery to dream and to go for it. To say he’s been supportive is an understatement.

We love you Dad, thanks for doing this song with us!

Mona & Lisa

Teen 1960 het die bevolking op 125 mense gestaan wat 'n bestaan gemaak het as vissers en bestaansboere. In 1984 is die dorpie en omliggende plase onteien en ontruim en deur Krygkor oorgeneem. Dit sluit aan by die De Hoop-natuurreservaat.

Verskeie groot skepe het hier gestrand. Die bekendste was die Maid of the Thames in 1848 en die Willem de Zwijger in 1863.

description:

As die reën van stof en roet verby is
 en die rook verdwyn,
 sal daar in die sterrelose hemel
‘n neonboog verskyn

En kyk maar goed, want as jy hom vind,
vertel ek vir jou ‘n sprokie, my kind,
van ‘n skatkis, met ou kettings gebind,
aan die neonboog se punt.

Volg hom elke nag oor swart riviere,
oor kranse van beton;
as jy aanhou stap tienduisend ure,
al jy dalk daar kom.

Maar hier moet jy jou nimmer laat bind,
want so lui die ou, ou sprokie my kind;
As jy geluk en vreugde wil vind,
soek die neonboog se punt
Volg hom elke nag oor swart riviere;-
kyk nie één maal om.

Dalk vind jy die land van blou saffiere
en dalk ‘n brokkie son.

description:
Jakkie Louw:  "Die liedjie is geskryf vir 'n pêl van my wie se meisie kanker gehad het. In die musiekvideo word die storie van 'n verliefde jong man wat langs sy siek meisie in die hospitaal sit, uitgebeeld. Sy ly aan terminale kanker en hy vra haar wat hy vir haar kan doen. Sy sê dan "gee vir my 'n miljoen". Niemand praat ooit oor geld op hul sterfbed nie. So hy sê dan vir haar: "Ek sal poetry skryf oor jou mond en jou lyf. Ek sal liedjies dan maak en dit sing tot jy slaap . . . want vanaand soen ek jou in 'n nuwe taal vir ons gebore . . . met een miljoen woorde." Ek moes my hare afskeer vir die video, en die meisie wat die aktrise is in die video het ook haar hare afgeskeer".

WHO IS DALLIN HESS?

A brave 15 year old boy who was diagnosed with cancer in 2011

There is a gene missing in his family that fights off cancer. they have already had 3 deaths in the family. his mother Sydney survived breast cancer at age 12. Her younger sister Alexis died from cancer, and their father Travis died last April from his battle with cancer.

When Dallin got sick, his bucket list wish was to put on "Life" t-shirts and go into his town and give away lemons to strangers on the street. He was too sick to walk that day, so he stayed in the car and watched his whole family do it for him.

Dallins hope was to spread a message of hope to the world that no matter what life hands you, something sweet can come from something sour.

It truly was bittersweet. 4 days after Dallins lemon project, he passed away peacefully on Feb 19th, a few days after his 15th birthday.

Here's to the Dallin Hess's all over the world who despite pain and hardships are turning lemons into lemonade

As we're writing this, thick snowflakes are drifting by our window. That doesn't happen a lot here in England and it reminds us of the winters at home in Austria. Everything is quiet and making us feel a little melancholic. It kind of fits with the song we are sharing with you today, so we are embracing the sentimental feelings as we're sipping on our hot cup of tea and uploading this video :-)

How are you all feeling? How has the start of 2021 been for you? Are you happy and doing alright?

These past few weeks we have been busy preparing for some new Duo Session videos. As you might know, they are a series of stripped-back videos that we are releasing regularly over at the MLT Club: https://mlt1.uk/ytmltc

We also upload them on YouTube sometimes, and today we want to share with you a Duo Session of our original "Close To You".

It is a song we initially released on our album ORANGE as a full studio production, but this more "minimal" version with just the two of us is part of our first "The Duo Sessions" compilation album.

We hope you're having a lovely day and send big virtual hugs to you all,
Mona & Lisa

So far, only MLT Club Members will have seen the video for it as it was originally recorded as a Club exclusive. Today we want to share it with you all!

It's a sweet and nasty song ... enjoy! ;-)

- - - - - - - - - 


I'll Follow The Sun" has always been one of our favourite melodic Beatles songs. It sounds so simple at first listen yet it's anything but. The chords are complex, and the way the melody loops around when the verse repeats has always fascinated us. Add Paul's sweet voice and it's a timeless masterpiece.

We remember vividly a time, many years ago, when we were about 14 years old and riding on a bus through Austria on a group excursion with our grandparents and a whole bunch of their friends and their grandchildren. The two of us spent the entire ride in the last row listening to Beatles songs. It was at the height of our Beatle Mania phase when we were in the middle of discovering and devouring their entire back catalogue and learning all songs by heart. 

"I'll Follow The Sun" came on on our mp3 player (no iPhones back then), and we put it on repeat at least three times. Then we walked through the aisle of the bus to our grandpa, made him listen to the song, got our mp3 player back and continued our Beatles listening session while driving to some castle or museum - The Beatles seemed much more important at the time. Frankly, they still are! 😉

For some reason, it was especially important to us that our grandpa listened to that one song in particular, because we couldn't believe how beautiful it was and just had to share that with someone. He'd never heard it before but he said he liked it so we were satisfied. Mission accomplished.

Now we hope you like our humble take on it!

It was 50 years ago (on February 9th, 1964), during the Beatles' legendary first appearance on the American "Ed Sullivan Show" back in 1964, when there have been no major crimes reported in New York City between 8 - 9 pm, cause even the criminals seemed to join the estimated 73,700,000 viewers in 23,240,000 homes in the United States.

Exactly 50 years later they are still likely to be the most influential band that has ever existed. Without them, music wouldn't be the same and a whole lot of great bands just wouldn't exist.

Here is our take on one of the songs they performed at that show back then - "I Saw Her Standing There". Filmed during our performance at the BaBü in Wolkersdorf (Austria) on March 7th, 2013. It was a beautiful warm night in spring!

Thank you John, Paul, George and Ringo for evoking our deep passion for music and for changing the meaning of music forever. We also want to thank every other musician and artist who has the desire to give something to this world and believes in the power of artistry.

Stay groovy,
Mona & Lisa

Revolution has always stood out to us as a song with great, thoughtful lyrics, and it was a rather spontaneous idea to add it to our repertoire! Today, exactly 33 years ago, John Lennon was killed by what he despised the most, violence. What might have been the most tragic day in the history of music now lies years behind, but his and the Beatles' music still touches the hearts of so many people and inspires even the youngest generation!

This performance was filmed and recorded on the 28th of September 2013 at the Aera club in Vienna, where we had a freaking amazing time sharing the evening with our friends from "CRAESH". Mona is singing the lead vocals, Lisa is playing the solo guitar.

video_title: Daniel O'Connell - Society [Eddie Vedder Cover] - Performed at Craft Exchange open mic
description:
Whenever someone asks me why I host open mic nights, one of the first things I tell them is that it is not JUST abut the music. Don't get me wrong, The Music is top of the list, but in the end, it is about the PEOPLE who make the music, and the HUMANS who support these people.

That being said, I take great joy in seeing personal growth in the open mic musicians, on more than just a musical level. Take Daniel O'Connell for instance. Musically, he has grown in leaps and bounds since he started playing open mic. He has effectively taken a nice hobby, and turned it into a craft that he can use to entertain, and yes, even earn money. 
However, seeing him grow as a person has to be one of my personal open mic highlights. 
From a shy-guy-in-the-corner, to, well, a shy guy that is not afraid to get on stage, or even interact off-stage. Now for me as an off-the-charts extrovert, that is not an issue, but I can only imagine how much of a challenge it has to be for a very strong introvert like Daniel. 
So with this, I would just like to say that I am super proud of the bloke, and really look forward to seeing where The Music takes him!

video_title: Michael Jackson’s THRILLER Surprise Flashmob by Perpetuum Jazzile | Cinema Audience Had No Idea!
description:
“Thriller” is out now! 🖤
Our new cover is available on all major streaming platforms.
Listen here: https://bfan.link/thrllr

****
ABOUT THE VIDEO:

They thought they were only coming to the premiere of Michael… but then the legendary sound of “Thriller” filled the cinema.

At the grand Slovenian premiere of Michael, the highly anticipated film about the life and music of the King of Pop, the audience in Ljubljana’s Odiseja cinema got an unforgettable surprise even before the movie began.

Members of Perpetuum Jazzile were secretly sitting among the audience. As Michael Jackson’s iconic “Thriller” started playing, they rose from their seats one by one, microphones in hand, and slowly made their way toward the stage like zombies while performing the legendary moves inspired by the original music video.  

What started as a regular movie premiere turned into a full cinema flashmob tribute to one of the most influential artists of all time. The audience had no idea what was coming — and their reaction says it all.

Performed by: Perpetuum Jazzile
Song: Thriller – Michael Jackson
Arrangement: Samo Vovk
Location: Odiseja, Ljubljana, Slovenia
Occasion: Slovenian premiere of Michael
Choreography: Karin Ahčin and Nastja Vodenik
Video: Urban Budihna, Kristjan Kuzmanoski, Matic Kremžar, Samir Vučkić
Edit: Urban Budihna

***

Mislili so, da so prišli samo na premiero filma Michael … potem pa so kino dvorano napolnili legendarni ritmi skladbe “Thriller”.

Na veličastni slovenski premieri filma Michael, težko pričakovanega filma o življenju in ustvarjanju kralja popa, je obiskovalce ljubljanske Odiseje še pred začetkom projekcije čakalo posebno presenečenje.

Člani Perpetuum Jazzile smo bili skrivaj razporejeni med publiko. Ko se je začel ikonični “Thriller” Michaela Jacksona, smo z mikrofoni v rokah drug za drugim vstali s svojih sedežev in se kot zombiji počasi pomaknili proti odru ter ob tem izvedli legendarne gibe, navdihnjene z originalnim videospotom.

The earliest vocal version was recorded by Freddy Quinn in 1965 titled as "Spanish Eyes"; soon after its release, the single was pulled from the market when Polydor (Quinn's label) and Decca (Kaempfert's label) threatened to sue, claiming ownership of the song.
A version by Sergio Franchi with lyrics by Charles Singleton was recorded in late 1965 titled "Moon Over Naples", but did not chart.
It was a hit single in 1966 for Al Martino when a new set of lyrics were written by composer Eddie Snyder, now titled "Spanish Eyes". (All subsequent versions used this title, and now listed both Singleton and Snyder among the credits.) Released in late 1965 in the United States, this recording reached number 15 on the Billboard Hot 100[2] and spent four weeks atop the Billboard Easy Listening chart[3] in early 1966. This vocal version was also a hit in Europe, where it sold an estimated 800,000 copies in Germany[3] and made the UK Singles Chart twice, peaking at number 49 in 1970 and then reaching number five in August 1973.[4]
Andy Williams released a version in 1967 on his album, Born Free.
A cover by Willie Nelson and Julio Iglesias peaked at number 8 on the Billboard Hot Country Singles chart in 1988.[5]
In 2003 the Italian accordionist Beppe Junior performs an instrumental version included in the album Liscioterapia (Europlay, CD 0189).
Little Willie Littlefield recorded a version for his 1990 album Singalong with Little Willie Littlefield.
In 2013, vocal group Il Divo recorded a duet with British singer Engelbert Humperdinck.[6] Produced by Alberto Quintero, it was included in the album Engelbert Calling released September 30, 2014.[7]

The original Nilsen Brothers Pepe Ederer (1932), Gerd Gudera (1933) and Walter Leykauf (1942) came from a village in Oberpfalz. They performed as amateur singers at small and large events and also won a talent competition of the Bayerischer Rundfunk. They were then invited to the TV show Toi, Toi, Toi, hosted by Peter Frankenfeld. After a performance in Hamburg, they received various offers from record labels, but eventually it became the Cologne label Electrola. Their first German-language single, Tom Dooley, was produced in the fall of 1958 and hit the German charts in December, where they made it to 1st place. They were also represented in the slot machine market charts with a listing of 36 weeks, the youth magazine Bravo recorded the number for 28 weeks in its Musicbox chart from December 1958 to July 1959, of which twelve times at number 1. The song was also sung in the film comedy Always those Mädchen.

Until 1961 10 singles were recorded with Electrola, including songs with Boy Berger and Angèla Durand. The title Die Cowboys von der Silver Ranch, together with Angèle Durand, hit the charts (1960, 2nd place). Further chart successes were Tom Dooley II (1960, 40th place), Sacramento (1961, 22nd place) and Stielaugen-Tango (1962, 50th place). The title Aber dich gibt's nur einmal für mich, composed by Ederer, only entered the charts in Austria (1967, 9th place). After the expiry of the contract with Electrola, there were only brief commitments with the labels Ariola, Decca Records and Philips. Only in 1965 they got a long-term contract with the Duisburg label Populär, good for more than ten single productions. In addition, they also collaborated in various films.

video_title: Stille Nag - Germandt Geldenhuys (ft. Reynardt Hugo, Clint Brink, Ben Kruger & Paul Lückhoff)
description:
ⓒ Germandt Geldenhuys
Jy kan sekerlik saamstem: 2020 was ‘n tawwe jaar wat baie van ons se hoop weg gevreet het en gevolglik gaan hierdie Kersfees dalk ‘n bietjie meer gedemp wees, vir baie mense. 
Dit is presies waaraan ek gedink het op ‘n Maandagmiddag einde November toe iemand my daaraan herinner dat daar in die stil tye van die lewe ook wonderwerke kan gebeur - dat nuwe lewe (en hoop) uit die eenvoud kan spruit. 
Ek het toe besluit ek wil “Stille Nag” (my ma se gunsteling Kerslied) opneem en vrystel oor die feestydperk.
Ek het dadelik my vriend (en maestro!), Sean Butler, genader om die opname te behartig. (Al was die “deadline” letterlik 7 dae, het hy ingestem en tot in die middernagtelike ure gewerk.) 
Sean, daar is nie baie mense soos jy nie. Jy is ongelooflik. Baie dankie.

Ek wou graag ook vir ‘n slag iets saam my vriende doen - al was dit net iets klein - en ek besluit toe om van my vriende by Binnelanders saam te nooi om te kom saamsing!
Hierdie manne het almal binne sekondes “ja” gesê toe ek dit aan hulle voorstel en elke liewe een van hulle het uit hulle pad gegaan om van hierdie projek ‘n sukses te maak. 
Dankie manne. Ek is trots om julle my vriende en kollegas te kan noem.
Saam julle sal ek oorlog toe gaan. 

Ek het ook besluit dat ek hierdie projek alles ten bate van die Abraham Kriel Kinderhuis gaan doen. So, elke keer wat jy die song aflaai, koop, speel of share, doen jy dit met die wete dat jy ‘n klomp kinders se Kersfees en Nuwe Jaar ‘n klein bietjie lekkerder gaan maak. Al die opbrengs word net so aan hulle geskenk. 

Ek hoop julle geniet - en word geraak - deur hierdie weergawe van Stille Nag deur my, (Germandt Geldenhuys), Reynardt Hugo, Clint Brink, Ben Kruger en Paul Lückhoff. 
SHARE sover as wat jy kan, asseblief. 
Hoe meer mense luister hoe meer fondse samel ons in. En sodoende versprei ons sommer ook die Kersfeesgees!

description:
🎵 WIE IS EK?
’n Afrikaanse verwerking, geïnspireer deur Charlie Pride se “Who Am I”

Op versoek van Miems is hierdie lied in Afrikaans verwerk — ’n besondere liedjie wat my geïnspireer het om Charlie Pride se “Who Am I” se storie en gevoel in Afrikaans te vertolk en ’n eie betekenis daaraan te gee.

Soms is jy die een wat iemand optel wanneer hulle val… die een wat daar bly wanneer hulle deur moeilike tye gaan… maar later bly daar net een vraag oor:

Wie is ek?

“Wie Is Ek?” vertel die verhaal van iemand wat alles gegee het, liefgehad het met sy hele hart en daar was toe iemand hom nodig gehad het — maar uiteindelik moet besef dat hy dalk nooit die een was wat sy hart gekies het nie.

❤️ Vir almal wat al ooit gewonder het of hulle genoeg was…

Wie is ek?

Miems, baie dankie vir jou versoek en vir die inspirasie agter hierdie Afrikaanse weergawe. ❤️

Laat weet my in die kommentaar wat hierdie lied vir jou beteken. Ek lees graag julle boodskappe.

description:
Wanneer Nashville ontmoet op die stoep van 'n Suid-Afrikaanse plaashuis. Ella Langley se "country grit" smelt saam met Leli se lae mezzo-tekstuur vir 'n gestroopte, eerlike weergawe van hierdie legende. Geen produksie-truuks nie—net 'n kitaar, 'n kers in die venster, en die reuk van vars koffie.
FUNFACTS TO CONNECT THEMES
Acoustic Revival: Hierdie weergawe fokus op die "Acoustic Revival" kanaal-tema, waar die instrumentasie gestroop is tot net die essensie van country en folk.

Country Soul Food: Die lirieke verwys na die "magic" van die kombuis—'n universele country-tema wat Nashville se koringlande verbind met die vetkoek en melktert van 'n plaaskombuis.

Vocal Texture: Leli se gebruik van vocal fry en whispers in plaas van melodiese sang skep 'n intieme, "late-night radio" gevoel wat perfek pas by die country-genre.

The idea behind this cover is bringing up the question of musical eternality. We believe that Justin Timberlake's music is just as eternal as Bach's and is here forever. This music covers Timberlake's "Cry Me A River" in a never-heard way: Creating a crossover between urban R&B / Pop and authentic baroque music inspired by J.S. Bach (motifs of Bach's Toccata and Fugue in D minor BWV 565 were also used as part of the arrangement). This new music concept targets both classical music lovers and popular music fans and will hopefully will bring them closer together. 

All music and sounds you hear are recorded, produced and performed by Bence, including his beatbox tracks and percussive sounds using the body of a grand piano. The classical elements and instrumental interludes were also arranged by Bence, creating over 100 different tracks, which were all mixed and mastered by him.

Sweet dreams till sunbeams find you …

Count On Me - MonaLisa Twins (Original Song)

-------------

No matter how many turns a river makes …
This song was initially written and recorded for our album ORANGE. It being a very “acoustic-y” song to begin with, it was the perfect candidate for a Duo Session. 

It’s about the thing that fundamentally keeps us going. The feeling of hope and meaning we derive from being there for one another, from helping each other for some sort of greater purpose. It’s about believing in life, believing in people, believing in yourself and in the journey you are on. Believing in the fact that things will work out.

Because as John Lennon once said: “Everything will be okay in the end. If it’s not okay, it’s not the end.”

3 ARTISTS COME TOGETHER FOR 3 CAUSES

This song was originally put together as a tribute to the lives lost in Kenya during the garissa attacks, and also the nigerian girls who were kidnapped. In light of the tragedies in paris, we add our prayers for the lives of those who were killed and also heavenly solace for families left behind to mourn for their beloved..

3 artists with African roots - Alex Boye' (Nigeria) Alisha Popat (Kenya) and Maia Von Lekow (Kenya) decided to get together to express their feelings the best way they know how - through music. This song stands for unity, resilience and is a video of remembrance for all those innocent people who are not with us today and who were taken from their families for no reason. It is a celebration of their lives and the Countries they called home.

Time for another video with our dear friend and huge musical influence, the one and only John Sebastian from the Lovin' Spoonful! Back when he flew over to visit us to record the music video for our single "Waiting For the Waiter" (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KCANQRkzKtY) we also made time for a few extra projects. One of this being a remake of one of our favourite Spoonful tracks "Did You Ever Have To Make Up Your Mind". 

We adore this song. Something about it always felt perfect to us ... the humor, the arrangement, the melody and lyrics with its tiny twists and turns. Such a well-crafted little gem.

The song is available on our album "MonaLisa Twins play Beatles & more Vol. 3" and now we also have this little video to go with it.

On the morning of Friday 2nd of March, i was invited to perform for a group of students at the Institute of Religion at Utah Valley University in Orem Utah.  It will be a day that will not easy be forgotten. Before i got up to give my presentation, a choir filed neatly into position behind me and began to sing. From the first note, all my senses was grabbed hold upon by a heavenly sound that left me breathless. I had to do a 360 turn to see who it was singing. I didn't take my eyes off them until they had finished. By the end, i was overcome with tears. It's lucky i don't wear mascara

video_title: Ye Oyo (Here she is) - Moise Mbiye | Lyrics in English | ft. Gabriel Okota | A Natsa Creations Film
description:
Here's an extract with Lyrics from my cover of Moise Mbiye's song Ye Oyo (Here she is) Covered by Jonathan Kalombo ft  Gabriel Okota on Guitar. 

Please do subscribe. Thank you for watching, stay blessed!!!

Translation of Song meaning (comes from the original video, link at the bottom):
English:
The song is the story of a person who is presenting to God a person who is not perfect, but his/her heart loves and asks God to change this person so that his/her love's weaknesses become strengths.
They also that their family  supports them so they stay together in peace for a long time. They also ask the church to pray for them so they can be blessed.
The chorus translates pretty much as I have sung it in English:
"Here she is, my lover, here she is, I dreamt it in a dream, my prayers have been answered hey, Here she is no more hiding, here she is, despite the struggles here she is..."

French:
La chanson est l'histoire d'une personne qui présente à Dieu quelqu'un avec des défauts, mais dont le coeur aime; afin qu'Il fasse grâce en transformant  ses faiblesses en force. 

Ensuite c'est à la famille qu'elle fait les présentations  en leur demandant de les aider à rester longtemps ensemble et en paix. C’est à l’église que les présentations s’achèvent, en leur demandant de prier pour eux afin d’être béni. 

Traduction refrain:

Le voici, c'est mon amour. Je l'avais vu dans mon rêve, ma prière a agit. 
Le voici, il n'y a plus des cachotteries, malgré les tempêtes, le voici.

____________________________________________________________

Auteur compositeur: Past. Moise Mbiye.

ABOUT WOUTER KELLERMAN
Globe-trotting flutist and composer Wouter Kellerman received a GRAMMY® Award for his album Winds of Samsara, also reaching #1 on the US Billboard Charts and peaking at #1 on the Zone Music Reporter Top 100 International Radio Airplay Chart.
 
His following album Love Language received a GRAMMY® nomination for Best Contemporary Instrumental Album. From the album, the song ‘The Long Road’, a solo flute piece which Wouter wrote for Nelson Mandela, won the 2016 Global Peace Song Award in the Acoustic/ Contemporary Music category. 
 
'Symphonic Soweto, A Tribute to Nelson Mandela' is a collaboration with the Soweto Gospel Choir and features the KwaZulu Natal Philharmonic and Angelique Kidjo. From the album, Wouter’s composition ‘Soweto Travels’ won first prize in the instrumental category of the 2018 USA Songwriting Competition. The album won the 2018 SAMA for ‘Best Adult Contemporary Album’. This was Kellerman’s seventh SAMA award, reinforcing his status as one of South Africa’s foremost musicians.
 
Wouter has performed all over the world in places like Berlin, Shanghai, Delhi and Sydney, including three sold-out concerts at Carnegie Hall in New York City. In 2010 he performed at the FIFA Soccer World Cup Closing Ceremony to a global audience of 700-million viewers.

Not all of us can do great things. But we can do small things with great love. — Mother Teresa.

'Symphonic Soweto' takes inspiration from the time of South Africa's oppression, the period of liberation and the journey between these - in short, telling the story of Soweto through its musical classics. By selecting from a historical repertoire, the trajectory of South African history is explored. This project strives to pave the way, musically, for the vision that Mandela had of social cohesion and tolerance. In Soweto, there is a tradition of storytelling in music: in this album, the choice of songs by popular musicians from the Apartheid era tells of a history of both struggle and ultimate celebration, while also recognising these musicians as part of our cultural, musical legacy.
'Symphonic Soweto' is the result of a powerful collaboration between two South African award-winning icons Wouter Kellerman and Soweto Gospel Choir, and features the country’s pioneer music ensemble, the Kwazulu-Natal Philharmonic Orchestra. This album represents the bringing together of two musical worlds in the city of Johannesburg, where historically the separation of Soweto under the former government prevented this: here music provides a common site of togetherness.

Given that this is a project about social cohesion, the album brings together a diverse range of musicians from South Africa and abroad. Mathebethebeni is from our new album 'Symphonic Soweto - Tribute to Nelson Mandela' with the Soweto Gospel Choir.

Mathebethebeni is a man named after a beautiful, colourful bird - a metaphor for freedom and diversity. The song speaks about how his Zulu dancing is so magnificent, it brings the memories of love and happiness alive. The music video is filmed at Constitution Hill (a former prison that incarcerated Mandela, and many other public figures) - an acknowledgement of the struggle for freedom and how these memories of better times were a way to survive the harsh realities of oppression.

It is a traditional Zulu song, originally arranged for the musical film Asinamali (‘We have no money’), directed by Mbongeni Ngema and Oscar-nominated Darrell Roodt. In the original setting Nelson Mandela, while on Robben Island, is in conversation with character Msizi Dube, of whom he requests to make a sacrifice for the people. The musical arrangement is a creative journey that brings about a fusion of African and Western Classical sounds and nuances.

description:
🔔Subscribe and click on the bell to be notified of all videos! 🔔
SPOTIFY: https://open.spotify.com/track/7JSNJCJ5lPCH44pEsOU9vj
'The Long Road' for Nelson Mandela by Wouter Kellerman (flute) is from the Grammy® nominated album 'Love Language'.

Buy 'The Long Road' on iTunes: http://tinyurl.com/cew2ksn

Available on Bandcamp: http://kellerman.bandcamp.com/track/the-long-road
This is the middle section of a piece I wrote for Nelson Mandela -- as a tribute to Nelson Mandela, I wanted to paint his life with the colours of the flute. 

The middle section of the piece starts when he moves to Johannesburg and the peacefulness of nature makes space for a train of events that would take control of his life and gather a momentum of its own. The percussive nature of this section indicates the runaway train of events, and the bits of the flute/vocal percussion is indicative of the influence that Ghandi's idea of peaceful resistance had in his life at the time.

You can hear the full piece here:
https://soundcloud.com/wouter-kellerman/the-long-road

It starts with his childhood, growing up in rural Transkei, where he was very close to nature and spent time in the fields herding cattle. When writing the song, I was thinking of him sitting by his cattle, listening to the beautiful sounds of nature, which even then must have been tinged with a sense of sadness, showing what was to come in his life. 

In the last section he retires and finally has time to spend with his family and be peaceful again. The piece ends on an unfinished note, showing that even when his life is over, his influence and memory will carry on and sustain us far into the future.

This is one of my favourite tunes - it suits the feel of the series perfectly and makes you think of open spaces and far away lands :)

When I tried to record this the first time, I was very disappointed - it just didn't have that epic feel that strings seem to get, so I tried to do it in a way that would suit the flute and I added all the other flutes. Then I kept on changing things until it sounded ok..
